consensus_summary: Blind consensus: thorns/thistles/briers primarily symbolize the curse on creation from the Fall — sin's consequences, unfruitfulness, and divine judgment (Gen 3:17-18; Heb 6:7-8; Isaiah desolation texts) — with well-recognized context-specific alternatives: worldly cares/riches choking the word (Parable of the Sower), wicked or worthless people/rulers (Judges 9; 2 Sam 23; Matt 7:16), personal affliction (2 Cor 12:7), and Christ bearing the curse (crown of thorns).
book_summary: The book defines bramble/thorns as the curse-ground's fruitless growth, specifically identified as worldly care and deceitful riches that choke the word, offer false protection (Jotham's bramble shadow), and end in fire (Judg 9:15; 2 Sam 23:7; Heb 6:8).
consensus_core_identification: Curse of the Fall and its outworkings: sin's consequences, judgment, and unfruitfulness, with worldly cares, wicked people, and affliction as passage-specific applications.
book_core_identification: The curse-ground's fruitless growth specified as worldly care and deceitful riches that choke the word, give false protection, and terminate in fiery judgment.
boundary_disagreement: The book keeps the consensus root (Gen 3:18 curse-ground; Heb 6:8 cursing and burning) but promotes one consensus alternative — worldly cares and deceitful riches from the Parable of the Sower — into the defining content of the symbol, and folds the Judges 9 bramble (false protection) and 2 Sam 23 fire-end into a single unified arc. It omits (and by its tight definition implicitly excludes) other consensus-covered cases: the personal-affliction thorn (2 Cor 12:7), the crown of thorns as Christ bearing the curse, protective hedging (Hos 2:6), and curse-reversal texts (Isa 55:13).
material_contradiction: None. The book's identification is a synthesis and narrowing of elements the consensus already lists (primary curse meaning plus the 'worldly cares' and 'worthless ruler' alternatives); nothing in the book requires rejecting the consensus's central referent.
rationale: Both readings anchor the symbol in the Genesis 3 curse and Hebrews 6:8 rejection, so the central referent is preserved. The material difference is one of extension and precision: the consensus treats 'worldly cares and riches' as a locally dominant alternative within the Sower parable, while the book makes that content the essence of the symbol everywhere, tying in false protection (Judges 9) and fiery end (2 Sam 23:7; Heb 6:8) as the symbol's trajectory. This is a real boundary move — reclassifying an alternative as the core content and dropping other admitted cases — but not a replacement of the consensus identification, so REFINED rather than MATCH or DIVERGENT.
strongest_objection: One could argue this is simply MATCH, since every element of the book's definition (curse-ground, choking cares, worthless bramble, fire) appears in the consensus primary or its 'common' alternatives, and a compressed glossary line cannot be read as rejecting omitted cases like the crown of thorns or Paul's thorn.
